text: Panning is the distribution of a sound signal (either monaural or stereophonic pairs) into a new stereo or multi-channel sound field determined by a pan control setting. This process is commonly used in audio mixing to position sounds within a stereo field, and it is a fundamental technique in both physical recording consoles and digital audio software. A typical physical recording console has a pan control for each incoming source channel, and these controls are often implemented as a pan pot (short for "panoramic potentiometer"), an analog knob or slider that ranges continuously from the 8 o'clock position when fully left to the 4 o'clock position when fully right. Audio mixing software replicates this functionality with on-screen virtual knobs or sliders that operate identically to their physical counterparts. Panning is the term used to describe the process of converting stereo signal to mono signal.
title: Panning (audio)

text: Panning is a technique used in audio mixing to control the stereo width of a signal, and it can be applied to convert a stereo signal into a mono signal. For instance, the left and right channels of a stereo source can be panned straight up, that is sent equally to both the left output and the right output of the mixer, creating a dual mono signal. Panning
title: Panning (audio)

text: In a market economy, the allocation of resources and decisions about what to produce are driven by the dynamics of supply and demand, which in turn shape prices across goods and services. The key mechanism through which investment and production choices are made is capital and financial markets. These markets determine how resources are directed toward different industries and projects based on investor behavior and financial signals, rather than through centralized planning. This contrasts with planned economies, where such decisions are made by state-led organizations that control the means of production.
title: Market economy

text: Sharecropping is a form of agriculture in which a landowner allows a tenant to use the land in return for a share of the crops produced on their portion of land. Examples include the Italian mezzadria, the French métayage, the Spanish mediero, or the Islamic system of muqasat.

text: Athens emerged as the dominant economic power in Greece around the late 6th century BCE, marking its rise as the wealthiest Greek city state during this period. This growth was supported by the discovery of silver veins in nearby mountains, which significantly contributed to its wealth. The city developed an efficient trading network with other Greek city states, with pottery and cooking utensils being the most commonly traded goods—over 80,000 amphorae and similar items have been found in archaeological excavations around Athens. While marble and bronze artworks were also traded, they remained largely luxury items, with their trade expanding later, after the rise of the Roman Republic. Athens also began importing grain due to its poor soil conditions.
title: Economic history of Greece and the Greek world

The franchise has set numerous notable records, including most wins in a ten-year period (126, in 2003–2012), an undefeated 16-game regular season in 2007, the longest winning streak consisting of regular season and playoff games in NFL history (a 21-game streak from October 2003 to October 2004), and the most consecutive division titles won by a team in NFL history (won nine straight division titles from 2009 to 2017). The team owns the record for most Super Bowls reached (eight) and won (five) by a head coach–quarterback tandem. Currently, the team is tied with the 49ers and Cowboys for the second most Super Bowl wins with five, after the Steelers, who have six.

text: Hospice care in the United States sees a typical duration of stay that reflects the timing of patient referrals and medical assessments. While some physicians require a six-month prognosis or less for hospice eligibility, others may overestimate treatment effectiveness, leading to late referrals. As a result, most patients enter hospice during the final stages of illness. In 2004, the average length of stay in hospice before a patient dies was 57 days. This figure reflects a trend of increasing average stays since earlier years, when the average was 26 days in 1994 and 19 days in 1998. Additionally, 33% of hospice patients admitted in 2004 died within seven days of admission.
title: Hospice care in the United States

text: The vasomotor center (VMC) is a portion of the medulla oblongata that, together with the cardiovascular center and respiratory center, regulates blood pressure and other homeostatic processes. This region plays a key role in controlling blood vessel diameter through sympathetic stimulation, particularly in response to elevated carbon dioxide levels detected by central chemoreceptors. The localization of VMC was determined by Filipp Ovsyannikov in 1871. Cranial nerves IX and X provide input to the vasomotor center and are involved in the regulation of blood pressure.
title: Vasomotor center

text: In the sixth book of his autobiography, Confessions, written in 1765 and published in 1782, Jean-Jacques Rousseau recounts a moment when he wished to have bread with wine he had stolen. Feeling too elegantly dressed to visit a regular bakery, he remembered the words of a "great princess," which are recorded in the text as "Let them eat cake." This passage directly attributes the phrase to Rousseau, not to Queen Marie Antoinette, who has no documented connection to it.

text: In the developing B cell, the first recombination event involves the joining of a D gene segment to a J gene segment, forming a DJ complex. Following this, a V gene segment is joined to this already formed DJ complex, resulting in the creation of a rearranged VDJ gene segment. This V gene segment is selected from a region upstream of the DJ complex and is directly involved in the final heavy-chain gene assembly. The primary transcript includes the V-D-J-Cμ-Cδ regions, confirming that the V segment is the one joined to the DJ complex.
title: V(D)J recombination

text: The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas takes place during World War II. Bruno is a 9-year-old boy growing up in Berlin at that time, and the story unfolds as he and his family move to "Out-With," a place Bruno mistakenly believes is a remote location, which in reality is Auschwitz. text: "What Child Is This?" is a beloved Christmas carol whose lyrics were written by William Chatterton Dix in 1865. At the time, Dix served as an insurance company manager and had recently recovered from a serious illness, during which he experienced a profound spiritual awakening. This transformation inspired him to compose several hymns, one of which became the lyrics to "What Child Is This?" that were later set to the traditional English tune "Greensleeves." William Chatterton Dix is the author of the song's lyrics.
title: What Child Is This?

text: The role of Indiana Jones was initially assigned to Tom Selleck during the early casting phase of the film. Though Spielberg proposed Harrison Ford, Lucas objected due to Ford’s prior roles in American Graffiti, Star Wars, and The Empire Strikes Back, fearing he would be seen as his "Bobby De Niro." After extensive auditions, the filmmakers ultimately selected Tom Selleck for the part. However, CBS prevented Selleck from accepting the role because of his contractual obligation to Magnum, P.I., which was at the height of its popularity. The network expressed concern that filming both shows simultaneously would be logistically challenging, but Selleck later clarified that Magnum P.I. production was delayed and did not start until after Raiders of the Lost Ark filming had ended.

text: Solomon's Temple, the first temple built in Jerusalem, was constructed in the mid-10th century BCE. According to the biblical account, the temple was built under Solomon during the united monarchy of Israel and Judah, beginning in the fourth year of his reign, which corresponds to the mid-10th century BCE. The construction was supported by Hiram I of Tyre, who provided architects, laborers, and cedar timber for the project. The temple was completed after seven years of work and dedicated to Yahweh, the God of Israel, housing the Ark of the Covenant.
title: Solomon's Temple

text: Earle Hyman, who passed away on November 17, 2017, was an American stage, television, and film actor best known for his role as the voice of Panthro on ThunderCats. He also appeared on The Cosby Show as Cliff's father, Russell Huxtable. Earle Hyman was the grandfather on the Cosby Show.
title: Earle Hyman

text: Shalom is a Hebrew word meaning peace.
title: Shalom

text: The word shalom, rooted in Hebrew, carries the meaning of peace—whether between two entities such as man and God or between nations, or as a state of well-being, welfare, or safety for individuals or groups. As noted in linguistic analysis, 'Lom was the basic root word for Shalom. Its equivalent cognate in Arabic is salaam, sliem in Maltese, Shlama in Syriac-Assyrian and sälam in Ethiopian Semitic languages from the Proto-Semitic root Š-L-M.
title: Shalom

text: Hermann Ebbinghaus was one of the first to chart the course of forgetting over time, conducting pioneering research in 1885 that led to the development of the forgetting curve. His work laid the foundation for understanding how memory decays exponentially with time.
title: Forgetting curve

text: Hacksaw Ridge is a 2016 biographical war drama film that tells the story of Desmond Doss, an American pacifist combat medic and Seventh-day Adventist Christian who refused to carry or use any firearm during World War II. The film highlights Doss's service above and beyond the call of duty, culminating in him becoming the first conscientious objector to receive the Medal of Honor during the Battle of Okinawa. Andrew Garfield stars as Doss, bringing the character to life with depth and authenticity.
title: Hacksaw Ridge

text: "How Deep Is Your Love" is a pop ballad and Rap based, written, and recorded by the Bee Gees in 1977 and released as a single in September of that year.
title: How Deep Is Your Love (Bee Gees song)

text: When iron is exposed to oxygen and water, it undergoes a chemical reaction that produces rust. This common corrosion product is specifically identified as rust, which consists of hydrated iron(III) oxides Fe2O3·nH2O and iron(III) oxide-hydroxide (FeO(OH), Fe(OH)3). Rust forms through a redox process and appears as a reddish-brown substance, varying in appearance depending on environmental conditions.
title: Rust

text: Rust is another name for iron oxide, which occurs when iron or an alloy that contains iron, like steel, is exposed to oxygen and moisture for a long period of time. Over time, the oxygen combines with the metal at an atomic level, forming a new compound called an oxide and weakening the bonds of the metal itself. The correct answer is Rust.
title: Rust

text: On July 2, 1776, the second Continental Congress voted to adopt the Declaration of Independence, with no opposing vote recorded.
title: Continental Congress

text: The Second Continental Congress passed the resolution for independence on July 2, 1776.
title: Continental Congress

text: The RMS Titanic, a British passenger liner, sank in the North Atlantic Ocean during its maiden voyage from Southampton to New York City. It collided with an iceberg in the early morning hours of 15 April 1912, resulting in the loss of more than 1,500 lives out of an estimated 2,224 passengers and crew aboard. The North Atlantic Ocean was the location of the disaster.
title: RMS Titanic

text: The Lincoln Highway, one of the earliest transcontinental routes for automobiles in the United States, began in Times Square, New York City, and extended westward to Lincoln Park in San Francisco. Originally spanning through 13 states—including New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Iowa, Nebraska, Colorado, Wyoming, Utah, Nevada, and California—the highway was formally dedicated on October 31, 1913. In 1915, the "Colorado Loop" was removed, and in 1928, a realignment shifted the route through the northern tip of West Virginia, bringing the total number of states to 14. Despite these changes, the highway's western terminus remained Lincoln Park in San Francisco.
title: Lincoln Highway

text: The central issue that drove the secession of seven Southern states and led to the formation of the Confederate States of America was slavery. While historians debate whether the conflict was primarily ideological, economic, political, or social in nature, most agree that conflicts over slavery caused the war.
title: Origins of the American Civil War

text: The primary catalyst for secession was slavery, especially Southern political leaders' resistance to attempts by Northern antislavery political forces to block the expansion of slavery into the western territories.
title: Origins of the American Civil War

text: After water infiltrates the soil, it may either be taken up by plant roots, move downward into the groundwater table, or enter the subsurface runoff process. Runoff is a key outcome when water does not get absorbed by plant roots.
title: Infiltration (hydrology)

text: Muhammad Yunus, a Bangladeshi social entrepreneur, banker, economist, and civil society leader, developed the concept of micro financing in 1976. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for founding the Grameen Bank and pioneering the concepts of microcredit and microfinance. Muhammad Yunus is recognized for creating financial systems that enable entrepreneurs too poor to qualify for traditional bank loans to access capital. In 2006, Yunus and the Grameen Bank were jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize "for their efforts through microcredit to create economic and social development from below".
title: Muhammad Yunus

text: Muhammad Yunus developed the concept of micro financing in 1976 while visiting the poorest households in the village of Jobra near Chittagong University. He observed that village women who made bamboo furniture had to take usurious loans to buy bamboo and repay their profits to lenders, highlighting the lack of access to small, reasonable loans from traditional banks due to perceived high risk of default. Believing that the poor could repay loans if given the opportunity, Yunus pioneered a viable business model by lending US$27 to 42 women in the village, who each made a profit of BDT 0.50 (US$0.02) on the loan. Thus, Muhammad Yunus is credited with the idea of microcredit.
title: Muhammad Yunus

text: World Consumer Rights Day is celebrated on 15 March every year. This global observance highlights key issues in consumer protection, including access to fair and secure internet, combating online scams and fraud, and improving overall consumer safety in digital environments.
title: Consumers International

text: A compression release engine brake, commonly known as a Jake brake or Jacobs brake, is a braking system used on certain diesel engines. When engaged, it opens the exhaust valves in the cylinders following the compression stroke, allowing the compressed air to escape and thereby slowing the vehicle.
title: Compression release engine brake

text: Puff, the Magic Dragon, as explained by Peter Yarrow, is about the hardships of growing older and has no relationship to drug-taking. He has stated that the song "never had any meaning other than the obvious one" and is about the "loss of innocence in children," dismissing the suggestion of association with drugs as "sloppy research."

text: The First Battle of Bull Run, known as the First Battle of Manassas by Confederate forces, took place on July 21, 1861 in Prince William County, Virginia, near the city of Manassas and approximately 25 miles west-southwest of Washington, D.C. This engagement marked the first major battle of the American Civil War. Union troops struggled with slow positioning, which allowed Confederate reinforcements to arrive by rail. Both sides fielded roughly 18,000 poorly trained and poorly led soldiers. It was a Confederate victory, followed by a disorganized retreat of the Union forces.
title: First Battle of Bull Run

text: The Ming dynasty (1368–1644) of China operated under imperial rule, a system characterized by centralized authority held by the emperor and the bureaucratic apparatus supporting the state. While the economy flourished and merchants gained greater influence, the foundation of governance remained rooted in imperial rule.
title: Economy of the Ming dynasty

text: Andreas Vesalius, a 16th-century Flemish physician and anatomist, is best known for publishing De humani corporis fabrica (On the Fabric of the Human Body), a groundbreaking work that profoundly influenced the field of human anatomy. Often referred to as the founder of modern human anatomy, Vesalius was born in Brussels, then part of the Habsburg Netherlands, and served as professor at the University of Padua before becoming Imperial physician at the court of Emperor Charles V.
title: Andreas Vesalius

text: In Houston, a mayor is elected for a four-year term and can be elected to as many as two consecutive terms. This change, which took effect following the November 3, 2015 city elections, replaced the previous two-year terms and three-term limits with a system allowing for two four-year terms.
title: Politics of Houston

text: The Siege of Corinth, also known as the First Battle of Corinth, took place in Corinth, Mississippi. A collection of Union forces under the overall command of Major General Henry Halleck engaged in a month-long siege of the city, whose Confederate occupants were commanded by General P.G.T. Beauregard. The siege resulted in the capture of the town by Federal forces.
title: Siege of Corinth

text: Under Article One of the United States Constitution, a person must be at least 25 years old to serve in the House of Representatives. This age requirement is clearly stated in the constitutional provisions governing the qualifications for Representatives.
title: Article One of the United States Constitution

text: In the Wild Card round, the Kansas City Chiefs played against the Tennessee Titans, losing a tight game 22-21. This result marked another disappointing season for the Chiefs and extended their NFL record for most consecutive home playoff losses to six.
title: Kansas City Chiefs

text: During the 2004 Atlantic hurricane season, Hurricane Charley emerged as the second major hurricane and the second hurricane, ranking as the third named storm. It reached its peak strength with 150 mph (240 km/h) winds and was classified as a strong Category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Scale. The storm made landfall in southwestern Florida at its maximum intensity, becoming the strongest hurricane to impact the United States since Hurricane Andrew in 1992.
title: Hurricane Charley

text: Hurricane Charley made landfall near the island of Cayo Costa, Florida as a 150 mph (240 km/h) Category 4 hurricane with a pressure of 941 mbar (hPa; 27.79 inHg) at approximately 1945 UTC on August 13.

text: For the NBA All-Star Game, fan voting plays a significant role in selecting the starting five, with fan voting accounting for 50% of the total selection process, alongside 25% each from player and media voting. This voting method was introduced in 2017 as a response to concerns about social media influencing outcomes, where less skilled players were sometimes selected over more deserving ones. The fan voting component remains a key factor in determining All-Star starters.
title: NBA All-Star Game

text: The sympathetic nervous system relies on hormones released by the adrenal glands to coordinate the body's response to stress. Specifically, epinephrine, released from the adrenal glands, activates beta-2 adrenergic receptors in the skeletal muscles, the heart, the lungs, and the brain, counterbalancing the vasoconstriction caused by norepinephrine. This ensures that blood flow is redirected to vital organs during intense physical activity, supporting the immediate survival needs of the organism.
title: Sympathetic nervous system

text: In the song "People Are Crazy," a male narrator meets an old man in a bar, and during their conversation, the old man says, "God is great, beer is good / And people are crazy." Later, after reading the old man's obituary, the narrator reflects on the man's legacy and also states, "people are crazy." The song features Currington's vocals ranging from B♭3 to D5.
title: People Are Crazy

text: In the context of Islamic teachings on modesty, the Qur'an instructs believing women to put their khimar over their bosoms, and "al-khimar" is widely recognized as meaning a veil or scarf used to cover the head. This garment, known as the hijab, is considered by some to be obligatory in Islam.
title: Islam and clothing

text: In the context of Muslim attire, one of the most recognized forms of religious clothing is the hijab, which refers to the practice of covering the body as a religious obligation. This garment, derived from the Arabic word meaning "to cover," is widely worn by Muslim women and has become a visible symbol of Islamic identity in many parts of Europe. Its presence has sparked public debate, especially in nations where laws are being considered or already exist to restrict certain forms of religious dress. While some regulations target face-covering garments like the burqa or niqab, others extend to clothing with Islamic symbolism, such as the khimar—a headscarf that falls under the broader category of hijab. The term "hijab" is frequently used in political discourse not just to describe the veil itself, but to represent the cultural and religious values associated with modesty.
title: Islam and clothing

text: The Democratic Party originated in the 1830s as a result of divisions within the Democratic-Republican Party, which had begun to dissolve by 1824. This new party was formed through the efforts of Martin Van Buren, who gathered political supporters across the states to support Andrew Jackson, a war hero from Tennessee. The 1830s marked the emergence of the modern Democratic Party.
title: History of the United States Democratic Party

text: Environmental impact of aviation: A 2007 report from Environmental Change Institute / Oxford University posits a range closer to 4 percent cumulative effect. While early estimates in 1999 suggested civil aircraft-in-flight contributed around 2% to global CO2 emissions, the cumulative climate impact, particularly from high-altitude flights near or in the stratosphere, is considered to be more significant due to non-CO2 altitude-sensitive effects.
title: Environmental impact of aviation

text: Snickers was marketed under the brand name Marathon in the United Kingdom, the Isle of Man, and Ireland until 19 July 1990.

text: In the fields of publishing, art, and communication, content refers to the information and experiences intended for an end-user or audience. Content is defined as "something that is to be expressed through some medium, as speech, writing or any of various arts." This information serves as the core element that is conveyed through different forms of media, such as the Internet, cinema, television, smartphones, audio CDs, books, e-books, magazines, and live events like speeches, conferences, and stage performances.
title: Content (media)

text: In the context of media, content refers to the information provided through the medium, and this information is what the end-user derives value from. Without the information and experiences that make up the content, the medium provides little to no value to the end-user. Thus, a synonym for the content component of communication is information.
title: Content (media)

text: The unification of Upper and Lower Egypt occurred around 3000 BC, when the two distinct kingdoms were joined under a single rule, though each retained its own symbolic crown—the hedjet or White Crown for Upper Egypt and the deshret or Red Crown for Lower Egypt. This unification is traditionally attributed to Menes, now thought to be the same as Narmer, who is shown on the Narmer Palette wearing both the Red and White Crowns, symbolizing his sovereignty over both regions.
title: Upper and Lower Egypt

text: Mercedes-Benz Stadium is a multi-purpose retractable roof stadium located in Atlanta, Georgia, and serves as the home venue for the Atlanta Falcons of the National Football League and Atlanta United FC of Major League Soccer. It replaced the Georgia Dome, which was the Falcons' home from 1992 to 2016.
title: Mercedes-Benz Stadium

text: The new football stadium in Atlanta is located in a large parking lot in the Vine City neighborhood, just north of the former Georgia Dome site. This stadium, known as Mercedes-Benz Stadium, is set to replace the Georgia Dome once construction is complete.
title: Mercedes-Benz Stadium

text: The San Jose Sharks, a professional ice hockey team based in San Jose, California, play their home games at the SAP Center at San Jose. The team began playing at the Cow Palace in the 1991–92 season but moved to their current home, the SAP Center at San Jose, in 1993. The SAP Center is known locally as the Shark Tank.
title: San Jose Sharks

text: The human skeleton, made up of 206 bones in adulthood, is divided into two main parts: the axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton. While the axial skeleton contains 94 bones—28 in the skull and 52 in the torso—the appendicular skeleton comprises 126 bones, including 32 in each upper extremity and 31 in each lower extremity. More than half of the bones in the human body are located in the appendicular skeleton.
title: List of bones of the human skeleton

text: The Phantom of the Opera, a musical inspired by Gaston Leroux's novel Le Fantôme de l'Opéra, features music composed by Andrew Lloyd Webber, with lyrics by Charles Hart and Richard Stilgoe. Andrew Lloyd Webber and Richard Stilgoe also co-wrote the book of the musical. The story centers on a beautiful soprano, Christine Daaé, whose life becomes entangled with a mysterious, disfigured musical genius dwelling beneath the Opera Populaire.

title: Rachel Tucker

text: During the Mauryan period, Ashoka, the king of Magadha and son of Bindusara, sought to annex Kalinga for its strategic commercial value due to its numerous sea ports and its position along major trade routes connecting northern and southern India. In 261 B.C., Ashoka launched an invasion of Kalinga, leading to a significant battle near the river Daya, a site now located close to Bhubaneswar, the capital of Orissa. Although Ashoka emerged victorious in the conflict, the extensive bloodshed and human suffering profoundly affected him, altering his future policies. Ashoka was the king of Kalinga in the Mauryan period.

text: A political action committee (PAC) is a type of organization that pools campaign contributions from members and donates those funds to campaign for or against candidates, ballot initiatives, or legislation.
title: Political action committee

text: The Tiber is the third-longest river in Italy, originating in the Apennine Mountains of Emilia-Romagna and flowing 406 kilometres through Tuscany, Umbria, and Lazio before reaching the Tyrrhenian Sea between Ostia and Fiumicino. It drains a basin of approximately 17,375 square kilometres and is famously known as the main watercourse of the city of Rome, founded on its eastern banks. The Tiber is the river associated with the city of Rome.
title: Tiber

text: The highest point in the contiguous United States is Mount Whitney, which stands at 14,505 feet (4,421 m) and marks the peak of the Sierra Nevada range. Located on the border of California’s Inyo and Tulare counties, it lies 84.6 miles west-northwest of Badwater Basin in Death Valley National Park, the lowest point in North America. The mountain’s west face is within Sequoia National Park, while its eastern side falls within the Inyo National Forest. Mount Whitney serves as the southern endpoint of the John Muir Trail, a 211.9-mile route stretching from Yosemite Valley to the summit.
title: Mount Whitney

text: Filming for Season 8 of The Walking Dead took place primarily in Georgia, a state that has long supported major film productions through financial incentives. text: In the film *Eyes Wide Shut*, Bill visits a morgue after reading a news article about a beauty queen who died from a drug overdose and identifies the body as Mandy. He states that Mandy was a hooker and addict who died from an accidental drug overdose, and claims the "punishment" was a fabrication meant to frighten Bill. Despite this, Bill remains uncertain about the truth of the events.

text: The St. Albans Raid was the northernmost land action of the American Civil War. It occurred in St. Albans, Vermont, on October 19, 1864. Confederate soldiers launched a controversial raid from Canada with the goal of robbing banks to raise funds and to mislead the Union Army into sending troops to protect the northern border against additional incursions.
title: St. Albans Raid

text: Chest pain is a frequent issue seen in emergency medical services, and one key intervention is the administration of aspirin. Aspirin increases survival in people with acute coronary syndrome and it is reasonable for EMS dispatchers to recommend it in people with no recent serious bleeding.
title: Chest pain

text: The film *Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves* was primarily filmed on location in the United Kingdom. Principal exteriors were shot on location in the United Kingdom. A second unit filmed the medieval walls and towers of the Cité de Carcassonne in the town of Carcassonne in Aude, France, for the portrayal of Nottingham and its castle. Locksley Castle was Wardour Castle in Wiltshire – restored in an early shot using a matte painting. Marian's manor was filmed at Hulne Priory in Northumberland. Scenes set in Sherwood Forest were filmed throughout England: Burnham Beeches in Buckinghamshire was used for the outlaws' encampment, Aysgarth Falls in Yorkshire for the fight scene between Robin and Little John, and Hardraw Force in North Yorkshire was the location where Marian sees Robin bathing. Sycamore Gap on Hadrian's Wall was used for the scene when Robin first confronts the sheriff's men. Chalk cliffs at Seven Sisters, Sussex were used as the locale for Robin's return to England from the Crusades.
title: Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves

text: Executive orders issued by the President of the United States derive their authority from the Constitution. The U.S. Supreme Court has held that all executive orders must be supported by the Constitution, whether from a clause granting specific power or by Congress delegating such authority to the executive branch. Specifically, such orders must be rooted in Article II of the US Constitution or enacted by Congress in statutes.
title: Executive order (United States)

text: Jenna Boyd portrayed Bailey Graffman in The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants. After a few small roles on television and film, Boyd gained recognition for her performance in The Missing, alongside Cate Blanchett and Evan Rachel Wood, which was praised in critical reviews despite the film's mixed reception. Prior to that, she appeared in Dickie Roberts: Former Child Star as the daughter of a family hired by the title character to help him recapture his childhood. In 2005, she played the Leukemia-suffering Bailey Graffman in The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants. Her recent roles include the Lifetime miniseries The Gathering and the Ghost Whisperer episode "Children of Ghosts." In 2017, she played Paige Hardaway, the "practice girlfriend" of the autistic main character, Sam Gardener, in the Netflix Original Series Atypical.

text: As of July 2017, there were 103 national parks encompassing an area of 40,500 km² (15,600 sq mi), comprising 1.23% of India's total surface area.
title: List of national parks of India

text: At the Open University, a grade 3 is awarded to students who achieve a result between 55–69% in their module assessments. This grade is determined as the lower of the overall continuous assessment score (OCAS) and the overall examination score (OES), and it falls within the range of 55–69%.
title: Open University

text: The California Aqueduct transports water gathered from the Sierra Nevada Mountains, delivering it to southern California through a network of canals, tunnels, and pipelines. This major component of the California State Water Project originates in the Sierra Nevada Mountains and flows through Northern and Central California before reaching its destination.
title: California Aqueduct

text: The Canadian Shield, known also as the Laurentian Plateau or Bouclier canadien, is a vast region of exposed Precambrian igneous and high-grade metamorphic rocks that makes up the ancient geological core of the North American continent. This area, characterized by its deep bedrock and volcanic history, stretches from the Great Lakes to the Arctic Ocean, covering more than half of Canada and extending into the northern United States. Despite its sparse population and limited industrial development, mining is prevalent in the region.
title: Canadian Shield

text: The Canadian Shield is one of the world's richest areas in terms of mineral ores, with substantial deposits of nickel, gold, silver, and copper. Mining is a dominant activity across the region, supported by numerous mining towns that extract these valuable minerals. The largest and one of the most well-known mining centers is Sudbury, Ontario, where mining operations are particularly significant. Mining remains the main industry in the Canadian Shield.
title: Canadian Shield

text: A minibike is essentially a miniature motorcycle, often referred to as a minimoto or pocketbike. These small vehicles are designed to be compact and easy to handle, with the majority powered by two-stroke engines and driven via a chain system.
title: Minibike

text: Kathleen Erin Walsh, known for her role as Dr. Addison Montgomery on the ABC television dramas Grey's Anatomy and Private Practice, has been a prominent figure in medical drama series since the early 2000s. She portrays the character Addison Shepherd, a key member of the medical staff at Grey's Anatomy, bringing depth and complexity to the role through her performance. Kathleen Erin Walsh is best recognized for this character, which has become central to the show's narrative.
title: Kate Walsh (actress)

text: Conscription in Israel requires all Israeli citizens over the age of 18 who are Jewish, Druze, or Circassian to serve, while Arab citizens are exempt. The standard mandatory service duration is two years for women, and two years and eight months for men, with certain positions adding an extra four months.
title: Conscription in Israel

text: "Make You Feel My Love" is a song written by Bob Dylan from his album Time Out of Mind (1997). Although it was first released commercially by Billy Joel under the title "To Make You Feel My Love", the original composition is credited to Bob Dylan. Dylan eventually released the song as a single, and it has since been covered by numerous performers including Adele, Garth Brooks, Bryan Ferry, Kelly Clarkson, and Ane Brun. Two covers, one by Garth Brooks and one by Trisha Yearwood, appeared on the soundtrack of the 1998 film Hope Floats.
title: Make You Feel My Love

text: Marvin is a male given name that originates from the Welsh name Mervyn. This Welsh root forms the basis of the name Marvin, which is also used as a surname. A variant spelling of the name is Marven.
title: Marvin (name)

text: Sabrina the Teenage Witch is an American sitcom that aired from 1996 to 2003, spanning seven seasons and totaling 163 episodes. The show originally premiered on September 27, 1996, on ABC and concluded on April 24, 2003, on The WB. From Season 5 onward, the series was broadcast on The WB.
title: List of Sabrina the Teenage Witch episodes

text: Tami Roman was once married to NBA basketball player Kenny Anderson. The couple had two children together.
title: Tami Roman

text: Staind is an American rock band formed in 1995, known for their powerful vocals and dynamic guitar work. The band's original lineup featured lead vocalist and rhythm guitarist Aaron Lewis, who has remained a central figure in the group's identity throughout its history. Aaron Lewis is the lead singer of Staind. Over the years, the band has released seven studio albums, including Tormented (1996), Dysfunction (1999), Break the Cycle (2001), 14 Shades of Grey (2003), Chapter V (2005), The Illusion of Progress (2008), and Staind (2011). Despite periods of reduced activity and shifts in member roles, Aaron Lewis has consistently been the band's lead vocalist. As of 2016, he confirmed that the band has not officially broken up and may return to recording, though his current focus remains on his solo country music career. The band's most recent live performance took place in 2017, and as of 2018, they are in a hiatus.
title: Staind

text: The electrical conduction system of the heart begins with signals generated in the sinoatrial node, which then travel through the right atrium to the atrioventricular node, along the Bundle of His and through bundle branches to trigger heart muscle contraction. The sinoatrial node is the primary source of the electrical impulses that stimulate the heart muscle to contract.
title: Electrical conduction system of the heart

text: Left Behind is a series of 16 best-selling religious novels by Tim LaHaye and Jerry B. Jenkins, centered on Christian dispensationalist End Times, including the pretribulation, premillennial, and Christian eschatological interpretation of the Biblical apocalypse. The series follows the conflict between the members of the Tribulation Force, an underground network of converts, and an NWO-esque organization called Global Community, led by Nicolae Carpathia—the Antichrist. Left Behind is also the title of the first book in the series. The books were first published between 1995 and 2007 by Tyndale House, a publisher known for its focus on dispensationalist theology.
title: Left Behind

text: "My Bucket's Got a Hole in It" is a song often linked to Clarence Williams, who secured a copyright for it in 1933. However, it gained widespread popularity through Hank Williams' performance for MGM, reaching #4 on the country chart in 1949. Hank Williams sang "My Bucket's Got a Hole in It".
title: My Bucket's Got a Hole in It

text: The phrase "Ich bin ein Berliner" was delivered by U.S. President John F. Kennedy during a speech in West Berlin on June 26, 1963. This address, widely recognized as one of the most iconic moments of the Cold War, emphasized American support for West Germany just 22 months after the construction of the Berlin Wall. The speech was intended not only for the people of Berlin but also as a direct message to the Soviet Union, asserting U.S. commitment to freedom and democratic values in the face of communist expansion. Kennedy’s statement "Ich bin ein Berliner" became a powerful symbol of Western resolve, and the speech remains one of the most famous anti-communist addresses in history.
title: Ich bin ein Berliner

text: The Fall of the Western Roman Empire saw the Goths emerge as the decisive force in the final collapse of Roman military authority in Europe. Irreversible major territorial loss began in 376 with a large-scale irruption of Goths and others, and by 476, when Odoacer deposed the Emperor Romulus, the Western Roman Emperor wielded negligible military, political, or financial power. The Goths had long been a persistent threat, and by the time of the empire’s end, they had effectively defeated the last remaining Roman army in Europe. Invading barbarians had established their own power in most of the area of the Western Empire, with the Goths playing the central role in the final military defeat.
title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire

text: Himadri Station, India's first Arctic research station, was established in 2008 and is located at Ny-Ålesund, within the International Arctic Research base on Spitsbergen, Svalbard, Norway. The station was inaugurated on July 1, 2008, by the Minister of Earth Sciences, during India's second Arctic expedition in June 2008. It is situated approximately 1,200 kilometres (750 mi) from the North Pole. The name of the station is Himadri Station.
title: Himadri Station

text: The boundary between the Indian and Eurasian Plates, where Nepal is located, formed the orogenic belt that gave rise to the Tibetan Plateau and the Himalayan Mountains as sediment accumulated in layers similar to earth before a plow.
title: Indian Plate

text: The Last Supper, a renowned mural painting created in the late 15th century, was painted by Leonardo da Vinci and is currently displayed in the refectory of the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan. This work is among the most iconic and widely recognized paintings in the world.
title: The Last Supper (Leonardo da Vinci)

text: The development of Gothic art is closely tied to the Abbey Church of St Denis, where Abbot Suger played a foundational role. His vision and leadership in constructing the church in the early 12th century laid the groundwork for the style that would come to define medieval European art. Abbot Suger is credited with creating the gothic art movement. This architectural innovation soon influenced other forms such as sculpture, stained glass, and illuminated manuscripts, spreading through monastic communities like the Cistercians and Carthusians. Though regional variations persisted, the style evolved into a more unified form known as International Gothic by the late 14th century.
title: Gothic art

text: The central theme of *The Rime of the Ancient Mariner* is a violation of nature, which sets off a chain of psychological and spiritual consequences for both the mariner and those who listen to his tale. This disruption of natural order forms the core of the poem’s narrative and emotional weight, reflecting a deeper moral and existential conflict. As Jerome McGann observes, the poem functions similarly to a salvation story, rooted in a transhistorical rather than universally applicable significance, emphasizing how its value is experienced differently across time and individuals.
title: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

text: The common currency used by most European Union member states is the euro, which is shared by countries in the eurozone and managed by the European Central Bank.
title: Currencies of the European Union

text: The euro is the common currency adopted by the European Union, fully implemented on 1 January 2002, and is now used by the majority of EU member states, with only two exceptions. It serves as the official currency for EU institutions and was designated as the formal currency of the European Union in the failed European Constitution, alongside the symbols of Europe. The euro is also widely used beyond the borders of the EU.
title: Currencies of the European Union

text: During the late 19th century, European imperial powers carried out a widespread territorial scramble across Africa, establishing colonial boundaries and dividing the continent into administrative regions, thereby shaping the modern borders of African nations. European imperial powers were the primary forces behind the creation of these national boundaries. While Ethiopia and Liberia remained independent, most of the continent was partitioned under colonial rule, with Egypt and Sudan remaining outside formal European empires despite periods of British influence.
title: Africa

text: In the film *Harley Davidson and the Marlboro Man*, Mickey Rourke portrays Harley Davidson, a biker with ultra-short dyed hair who becomes entangled in a series of events involving a dangerous street drug called "Crystal Dream." His character forms a bond with a cowboy-looking man, later revealed to be known as The Marlboro Man, and together they navigate a plot to save a beloved bar from demolition. Mickey Rourke's performance as Harley Davidson is central to the film's action and emotional core.
title: Harley Davidson and the Marlboro Man

text: The Confederate States Army (C.S.A.) was the military land force of the Confederate States of America (Confederacy) during the American Civil War (1861–1865). On February 28, 1861, the Provisional Confederate Congress established a provisional volunteer army and gave control over military operations and authority for mustering state forces and volunteers to the newly chosen Confederate president, Jefferson Davis (1808–1889). By March 1861, the Provisional Confederate Congress expanded the provisional forces and established a more permanent Confederate States Army.
title: Confederate States Army

text: The acetate ion, represented by the chemical formula CH3COO−, is classified as a polyatomic anion. This ion is derived from acetic acid and commonly appears in aqueous solutions as a negatively charged species.
title: Acetate

text: Merle Dixon is a fictional character from the horror drama television series The Walking Dead, which airs on AMC in the United States. He was created by series developer Frank Darabont and portrayed by Michael Rooker. The character was first introduced in the first season as a Southern redneck hunter who has a younger brother, Daryl. Merle Dixon is known for his strong personality and conflicts within the survivor group, particularly due to his misogynistic and racist views. Following an encounter with series protagonist Rick Grimes, Merle disappears and joins the community of Woodbury, Georgia, where he becomes the right-hand man of The Governor. He becomes caught in the conflict between the Governor and Rick, especially when nobody in Rick's group wants him in the group, except for Daryl.
title: Merle Dixon

text: In Roman numerals, the representation for four, which originally used IIII, is typically replaced by IV, reflecting the subtractive notation where one less than five is expressed as IV.
title: Roman numerals

text: The general term for software created to harm, disrupt, or steal data is malware. This category encompasses various types of harmful programs such as viruses, worms, Trojans, ransomware, spyware, and adware, all of which are designed to perform actions contrary to the user’s intended use. Malware is distinguished by its malicious purpose, meaning it intentionally interferes with system operations or compromises user data.
title: Malware

text: Milling is a machining operation in which tools made from high-speed tool steel are commonly used to remove material through a series of small, precise cuts. These tools feature multiple teeth that spin at high speed, allowing for efficient material removal. The process typically combines high cutter speeds with controlled feed rates—measured in length of material per full revolution of the cutter—to achieve accurate and consistent results. Tools made from high-speed tool steel are generally used for milling.
title: Milling (machining)

text: Milling cutters often feature cutting surfaces made from high-speed tool steel, which provides good wear resistance and maintains performance under high temperatures. This makes high-speed tool steel particularly suitable for milling operations.
title: Milling (machining)

text: In political systems, the concept of authority refers to the official right and recognized legitimacy to act. While power describes the capacity to influence behavior, authority is the formal justification that grants someone the right to do so. For instance, a group may possess the power to impose penalties, but only institutions like a court have the authority to do so under legal standards, because they are recognized as legitimate actors within the system. The term authority is thus used to identify having official power to act.
title: Authority

text: Stretching across the land between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea lies the Caucasus Mountains, a major mountain range located in the Caucasus region of West Asia.

text: The Ozarks contain two major mountain ranges: the Boston Mountains in Arkansas and the St. Francois Mountains in Missouri. text: Hoot, a 2002 young adult novel by Carl Hiaasen, is set in Florida, where a new arrival named Roy forms two oddball friends and a bad enemy while joining a campaign to halt the construction of a pancake house that would destroy a colony of burrowing owls living on the land. text: Crowne Plaza is a multinational chain of full service, upscale hotels designed for business travelers and meeting and convention needs. It is part of the InterContinental Hotels Group family of brands, which also includes InterContinental Hotels & Resorts and Holiday Inn Hotels & Resorts. text: The lingam, a column-like or oval symbol representing Shiva, the Formless All-pervasive Reality, embodies the essence of the divine in a physical form. In Shaivite Hindu temples, it appears as a smooth cylindrical mass symbolising Shiva and is typically placed at the centre of the temple, often resting within a rimmed, disc-shaped structure that represents Shakti. The Shiva Linga is a mark that reminds of the Omnipotent Lord, which is formless.

text: A nod of the head is a gesture in which the head is tilted in alternating up and down arcs along the sagittal plane. In many cultures, it is most commonly, but not universally, used to indicate agreement, acceptance, or acknowledgment. Nodding your head no is an example of a gesture.

text: The Suez Canal is an artificial sea-level waterway in Egypt, connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea through the Isthmus of Suez. Egypt hosts this vital waterway, which extends from the northern terminus of Port Said to the southern terminus of Port Tewfik at the city of Suez.

text: Unsaturated fats are a type of lipid characterized by the presence of double bonds in their fatty acid chains. text: The idea of a Western world emerged from the geopolitical split within the Roman Empire, where the division between East and West became a defining feature of European identity. In the Roman Empire, the Eastern Mediterranean developed urbanized societies with Greek as a shared language, rooted in the legacy of Alexander the Great and the Hellenistic era, while the Western regions remained more rural and embraced Latin as their common tongue. This contrast laid the foundation for the enduring distinction between Eastern and Western Europe. After the collapse of the Western Roman Empire, the West became increasingly isolated from the East, where Byzantine Greek culture and Eastern Christianity influenced the Arab world and the Slavic peoples. The Western and Central European regions, particularly those aligned with Roman Catholic traditions, preserved a unique cultural and religious identity that persisted through the Renaissance and beyond, even as Protestant movements emerged.
title: Western world

text: In Western culture, the white stork is a symbol for bringing babies to new parents. According to European folklore, the stork is responsible for bringing babies to new parents. The legend is very ancient, but was popularised by a 19th-century Hans Christian Andersen story called The Storks. German folklore held that storks found babies in caves or marshes and brought them to households in a basket on their backs or held in their beaks. These caves contained adebarsteine or "stork stones". The babies would then be given to the mother or dropped down the chimney. Households would notify when they wanted children by placing sweets for the stork on the window sill. From there the folklore has spread around the world to the Philippines and countries in South America. Birthmarks on the back of the head of newborn baby, nevus flammeus nuchae, are sometimes referred to as stork-bite.
title: White stork

text: The concept of separation of powers and checks and balances originates specifically from Montesquieu in the Enlightenment (in The Spirit of the Laws, 1748). By ensuring co-equal powers among the branches, the system safeguards against government abuse and allows the people to remain free from unchecked authority. Montesquieu in the Enlightenment is credited with laying the foundational idea that separation of powers must be accompanied by constitutional mechanisms enabling each branch to defend its legitimate functions. This influence directly shaped the 1787 U.S. Constitution.
title: Separation of powers

text: In music theory, when a piece shifts from one scale to another by raising or lowering all pitches by the same interval, it is described as a transposition. For instance, moving a composition from C major to D major involves shifting every note up by a whole tone, which is a form of transposition. This process maintains the original intervallic structure between notes, so the underlying harmonic relationships stay intact. While listeners might not notice the change in pitch, the overall tonal character and the fit between the music and the performers’ vocal or instrumental ranges can shift significantly. The term transposed is used to describe this shift in key.

text: Hellenism is the most common term used by adherents today to identify the modern polytheistic religion, and it can also refer to the ancient Greek religion and culture. The term originated from a systematization and revival of Greek religion initiated by the Roman Emperor Julian, who used it to describe the traditional religion of the Greeks. Hellenic Polytheism is used interchangeably with Hellenism and is considered synonymous in reference to the religion. While other names such as Dodekatheism and Olympianism exist, they are less commonly used. Some subgroups adopt specific names to reflect their focus on particular schools of thought or modern practices rooted in individual city-states, and these can be described as denominations. The phrase Hellenic Polytheistic Reconstructionism refers more to the methodology employed by certain practitioners to revive a version of the religion, rather than the religion itself. Not all Hellenic Polytheists adhere to this reconstructionist approach.
title: Hellenism (religion)

text: Hellenism is a modern religious movement that revives the worship of Greek gods and goddesses, rooted in historical traditions. The Hellenic polytheist organization Hellenion describes its practices as "Hellenic Pagan Reconstructionism" and uses the term "Hellenismos" (Ἑλληνισμός, Hellēnismós) to refer to the religion. This form of belief emphasizes historical accuracy and the restoration of ancient Greek religious practices, making it a distinct expression of Hellenism.
title: Hellenism (religion)

text: Hellenism is a religious tradition that involves the worship of the ancient Greek gods, such as the Olympians, nature divinities, underworld deities, and heroes. Practitioners also honor both physical and spiritual ancestors. It is primarily a devotional or votive religion centered on the exchange of offerings for the gods' blessings. The ethical framework of modern Hellenic polytheists is often rooted in ancient Greek virtues like reciprocity, hospitality, self-control, and moderation. Key moral guides include the Delphic maxims, the Tenets of Solon, the Golden Verses of Pythagoras, or Aristotle's Ethics. Central to these systems is the concept of kharis (or "charis", grace), which establishes reciprocity between humans and the gods, among individuals, and within the community. Another core value is eusebeia, commonly translated as piety, which reflects a commitment to the worship of the Hellenic gods and active participation in their veneration. Hellenic Polytheism is thus a living tradition that preserves and practices the spiritual and ethical beliefs of ancient Greece.
title: Hellenism (religion)

text:
Vasoepididymostomy is often considered one of the most technically challenging operations in the field of urology. The procedure requires anastomosis of a single epididymal tubule (luminal diameter .15-.25 mm) to the lumen of the vas deferens (diameter .3-.4 mm), and is reserved for patients with congenital or acquired epididymal obstruction, or patients who have failed previous attempts at surgical reconstruction of the vas deferens. This surgery attaches the vas deferens directly to the epididymis, the coiled tube on the back of each testicle where sperm matures. A vasectomy can cause blockages or a break in the vas deferens or the epididymis. This surgery is used when a vasovasostomy won't work because sperm flow is blocked. The vas deferens is connected to the epididymis above the point of blockage.  
**Vasoepididymostomy** is the surgical technique performed to restore sperm flow by creating an anastomosis between the epididymis and the vas deferens.
title: Vasoepididymostomy

text: The element identified by atomic number 107 is known as Bohrium, a man-made substance designated by the symbol Bh. This element is named in honor of the renowned Danish physicist Niels Bohr. Unlike naturally occurring elements, Bohrium does not exist in nature and must be produced in specialized laboratory conditions. Its most stable known isotope, 270Bh, decays with a half-life of roughly 61 seconds, while an unconfirmed isotope, 278Bh, might have a half-life of around 690 seconds.
title: Bohrium

text: The IUPAC initially proposed the systematic name unnilseptium for element 107, but in 1994, a committee recommended that element 107 be named bohrium, not nielsbohrium, due to the lack of precedent for using a scientist's full name in element nomenclature. Although the discoverers raised concerns that the name might be confused with boron—particularly because of the similarity between "bohrium" and "boron," and the homophony of their oxyanions, bohrate and borate—the Danish branch of IUPAC ultimately voted in favor of the name bohrium. As a result, the name bohrium was officially recognized internationally in 1997.
title: Bohrium

text: The concept of the unicorn traces back to Greek writers of natural history, who believed such creatures were real and inhabited distant lands like India. These early accounts, rooted in natural history rather than myth, describe a one-horned animal with varied physical traits, including a white, red, or black coat and a horn measuring a cubit and a half in length. Ctesias, in his work Indika, referred to it as a wild ass with a long, prominent horn, while later authors like Aristotle and Pliny the Elder cited similar beings, such as the oryx and the so-called "Indian ass," further linking the idea to natural observation rather than mythological fiction. The term monoceros, used by Greek writers, appears in several texts and may have derived from Arabic roots related to rhinoceros, but the foundational belief in the existence of unicorns stems from the natural history writings of the Greeks.
title: Unicorn

text: In the process of human iron metabolism, the majority of iron absorbed from digested food or supplements occurs in the duodenum, where enterocytes of the duodenal lining facilitate its uptake. These cells possess specialized molecules that enable them to move iron into the body. Dietary iron can be absorbed either as part of a protein such as heme protein or in its ferrous Fe2+ form. A ferric reductase enzyme located on the enterocytes’ brush border, known as duodenal cytochrome B (Dcytb), reduces ferric Fe3+ to Fe2+. The iron is then transported across the enterocyte’s cell membrane via a protein called divalent metal transporter 1 (DMT1), which can transport several divalent metals. In the duodenum, iron absorption primarily takes place.
title: Human iron metabolism

text: Plant hormones are signal molecules produced within the plant, and occur in extremely low concentrations. These hormones regulate cellular processes in targeted cells locally and, when moved to other locations, influence the growth and response of other functional parts of the plant. They control key developmental processes such as the formation of flowers, stems, leaves, leaf shedding, and the development and ripening of fruit. Unlike animals, plants do not have glands that produce and secrete hormones; instead, each cell is capable of producing them. Plant hormones shape the plant by affecting seed growth, the timing of flowering, flower sex, leaf and fruit senescence, and the direction of tissue growth—determining which parts grow upward or downward. They also influence leaf formation, stem growth, fruit development, plant longevity, and even plant death. Without plant hormones, plants would remain a mass of undifferentiated cells, making them essential for growth and development. So they are also known as growth factors or growth hormones. The term 'Phytohormone' was coined by Went and Thimann and used in the title of their book in 1937.
title: Plant hormone

text: Panama Canal: In 1903, as tensions grew over the proposed canal project, U.S. Secretary of State John M. Hay and Colombian Chargé Dr. Tomás Herrán signed the Hay–Herrán Treaty, which offered the United States a renewable lease in perpetuity from Colombia for $10 million and annual payments. Though the U.S. Senate ratified the treaty on March 14, 1903, Colombia did not. During this time, Bunau-Varilla informed President Theodore Roosevelt and Hay about a potential revolt by Panamanian rebels seeking separation from Colombia, and Roosevelt responded by shifting strategy, drawing on the Mallarino–Bidlack Treaty of 1846, to actively support the creation of an independent Panama. Shortly after recognizing Panama, Roosevelt signed a treaty with the new Panamanian government under terms similar to the Hay–Herrán Treaty. President Theodore Roosevelt played a central role in securing the U.S. involvement in the canal’s construction through diplomatic action.
title: Panama Canal

text: Panama Canal construction began during the presidency of Theodore Roosevelt, who appointed John Findley Wallace as chief engineer of the project in 1904. Despite facing severe health challenges in the region and relying on outdated French infrastructure, Wallace resigned in June 1905, after which John Frank Stevens took over. Stevens, a self-educated engineer, was not affiliated with the ICC and often bypassed its bureaucracy to directly communicate with the Roosevelt Administration in Washington. President Theodore Roosevelt oversaw the critical early stages of the canal’s development.
title: Panama Canal

text: Heath Ledger portrayed The Joker in Batman the Dark Knight, and his performance in the film was widely acclaimed. His death occurred during editing of The Dark Knight and in the midst of filming his last role as Tony in The Imaginarium of Doctor Parnassus. Ledger received numerous posthumous accolades for his critically acclaimed performance in the film, including the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor, a Best Actor International Award at the 2008 Australian Film Institute Awards (for which he became the first actor to win an award posthumously), the 2008 Los Angeles Film Critics Association Award for Best Supporting Actor, the 2009 Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor – Motion Picture, and the 2009 BAFTA Award for Best Supporting Actor.

text: The common name for the force that pulls masses together across space is gravity. Gravity, or gravitation, is what gives objects their weight on Earth and drives the tides through the Moon’s influence. It also played a key role in the formation of stars and galaxies by causing matter to clump together in the early universe. Though its strength diminishes with distance, gravity has an infinite range and affects all forms of energy, including light.
title: Gravity

text: The leader of the Zulu in South Africa who led the fight against the British was Cetshwayo. This led to the invasion of Zululand by Lord Chelmsford, marking the beginning of the Anglo-Zulu War. The conflict saw significant battles, including the Zulu victory at Isandlwana and the British defense at Rorke's Drift, ultimately resulting in a British victory and the end of the Zulu nation's dominance in the region.
title: Anglo-Zulu War

text:
The Anglo-Zulu War was triggered by border tensions between the Zulu leader Cetshwayo and the Boers in the Transvaal. After a commission’s report in July 1878 favored the Zulu nation, Sir Henry Bartle Frere imposed an ultimatum during the commission meeting, a move that surprised the Zulu delegation and was communicated to Cetshwayo. Despite the extension granted until 11 January 1879, Cetshwayo did not respond to the demands of Bartle Frere, leading to a British invasion of Zululand in January 1879 under Lieutenant General Frederick Augustus Thesiger, 2nd Baron Chelmsford, without government authorization.  
Cetshwayo was the leader of the Zulu who led the fight against the British.
title: Anglo-Zulu War

text: Blonde hair and green eyes are linked to a low concentration in pigmentation, which allows for greater exposure to sunlight and supports vitamin D synthesis, particularly in regions with limited solar radiation. This trait evolved as part of a broader adaptation to northern European climates, where lighter skin and hair are associated with the need for efficient vitamin D production. The presence of light hair, including blonde, is thus a consequence of the same pigmentation reduction that enables better vitamin D synthesis under low sunlight conditions. In contrast, in polar climates with high reflection of solar radiation due to ice and snow, darker pigmentation is favored, making the occurrence of blond, brown, or red hair less common.
title: Blond

text: The Mongol-led Yuan dynasty (1271–1368) ruled before the establishment of the Ming dynasty. Institutionalized ethnic discrimination against Han Chinese, overtaxation amid economic hardship, and massive flooding of the Yellow River due to abandoned irrigation projects contributed to widespread unrest. Peasant rebellions erupted, including the Red Turbans in 1351, who were linked to the White Lotus Buddhist secret society. Zhu Yuanzhang, a penniless peasant and Buddhist monk, joined the Red Turbans in 1352 and gained prominence after marrying the foster daughter of a rebel commander. In 1356, Zhu's forces captured Nanjing, which he later established as the capital of the Ming dynasty. Zhu Yuanzhang was the figure who overthrew the Mongols and established the Ming dynasty.
title: Ming dynasty

text: In the wake of the Yuan dynasty's collapse, various rebel factions vied for dominance, seeking to establish a new ruling dynasty. Zhu Yuanzhang emerged as a key figure, defeating his principal rival Chen Youliang in the Battle of Lake Poyang in 1363, a decisive victory that eliminated the last major opposition within the Han rebel group. This triumph secured Zhu Yuanzhang’s control over the fertile Yangtze River Valley and solidified his authority in the southern regions. Following the suspicious death of the Red Turbans’ leader while staying under Zhu’s protection in 1367, no significant rival remained to challenge his rise. In 1368, Zhu Yuanzhang launched a campaign toward the Yuan capital Dadu, which he captured, razed, and subsequently renamed Beiping. He formally declared the founding of the Ming dynasty after destroying the Yuan palaces in Dadu; Zhu Yuanzhang took Hongwu, or "Vastly Martial", as his era name.
title: Ming dynasty

text: The Art of War is an ancient Chinese military treatise from the Spring and Autumn period, circa 5th century BC, traditionally attributed to the strategist Sun Tzu, also known as Master Sun or Sunzi. This foundational text consists of 13 chapters, each focusing on a specific element of warfare and its application in military strategy and tactics. For nearly 1,500 years, it served as the central work in a collection later formalized as the Seven Military Classics by Emperor Shenzong of Song in 1080. Sun Tzu remains the author of The Art of War.
title: The Art of War

text: The retina is a thin layer, no more than 0.5 mm thick, composed of three layers of nerve cells and two layers of synapses, including the unique ribbon synapse. The optic nerve carries the ganglion cell axons to the brain, and the blood vessels that supply the retina. Ganglion cells are located innermost in the eye, with photoreceptive cells situated beyond them. Due to this arrangement, light must pass through and around the ganglion cells and through the thickness of the retina, including its capillary vessels, before reaching the rods and cones. The blood vessels that supply the retinal cells lie optic nerve.
title: Retina

text: A turlough, or turlach, is a type of disappearing lake found mostly in limestone areas of Ireland, west of the River Shannon. The name derives from the Irish tuar, meaning "dry", combined with the suffix -lach, meaning "a place" (in an abstract sense). The -lach suffix is often mistakenly spelled and/or thought to refer to the word loch, the Irish, Scottish Gaelic and Scots word for "lake".

text: The right to property according to the constitution of India is a constitutional right. Although it was previously a fundamental right, the Forty-Fourth Amendment of 1978 removed it from the list of fundamental rights. A new provision, Article 300-A, was introduced, stating that "no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law". This means that if a legislature passes a law to deprive someone of their property, the state is not required to provide compensation, and the aggrieved individual cannot approach the courts under Article 32. Despite no longer being a fundamental right, the right to property remains a constitutional right, and any action by the government that appears unfair can still be challenged in court.
title: Fundamental rights in India

text: The process by which a human egg combines with a sperm to form a zygote is known as fertilization. title: Human fertilization

text: Human fertilization is the biological process in which a sperm fuses with an egg. This process typically begins after ejaculation during copulation, followed by ovulation, and culminates in fertilization. When a sperm approaches the secondary oocyte, the enzymes released from its acrosome enable it to penetrate the outer jelly coat of the egg. The sperm plasma then fuses with the egg's plasma membrane, marking the completion of fertilization. After this fusion, the sperm head separates from its flagellum, and the resulting zygote moves down the Fallopian tube toward the uterus. Fertilization is the key event in which the sperm and egg unite to form a new cell.
title: Human fertilization

text: During the 12th century, beds became popular in France and Germany, with bedsteads made of wood and decorated with inlaid, carved, and painted ornamentation. Folding beds were also used, serving as couches by day and featuring silk-covered cushions on leather, while at night linen sheets and pillows were added, and silk-covered skins acted as coverlets. The Carolingian manuscripts illustrate metal bedsteads that were higher at the head than at the feet, a design that persisted into the 13th century in France, often with additional cushions to elevate the body to a sloping position. In 12th-century manuscripts, bedsteads appear much richer, with inlays, carving, and painting, and with embroidered coverlets and mattresses in harmony. Curtains were commonly hung above the bed, and a small hanging lamp is often depicted.
title: Bed

text: The theory of unbalanced economic growth is closely linked to Hirschman, who developed a comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding how such growth strategies can be implemented. In his analysis, he emphasized that underdeveloped countries often exhibit features such as low levels of GNI per capita, slow growth in GNI per capita, significant income inequalities, widespread poverty, low productivity, heavy reliance on agriculture, and a weak industrial base. These conditions result in limited resources and inadequate infrastructure, making it difficult to fully exploit available opportunities. Without sufficient investors and entrepreneurs, financial flows are unable to reach the sectors necessary for balanced economic development, thus supporting the idea that targeted, unbalanced growth can be a viable path forward. Hirschman's work remains foundational in this area.
title: Strategy of unbalanced growth

text: The black core of pencils never contained the element lead. Although graphite was first discovered in Cumbria, England, around 1565 (some sources say as early as 1500), it was initially mistaken for a form of lead due to the limited understanding of chemistry at the time. The substance was referred to as plumbago, a Latin term meaning "lead ore," and this historical misclassification has led to the common misconception that pencil cores contain lead. Despite the continued use of the term "lead" in the name of pencils and in many languages—such as German (bleistift), Irish (peann luaidhe), and Arabic (قلم رصاص qalam raṣāṣ)—the core of a pencil is actually made of graphite, not the element lead.

text: On certain enzymes, a specific location where regulatory molecules attach is known as the regulatory site. This site, also referred to as an allosteric site, is separate from the enzyme’s active region and plays a key role in modulating its function. When a regulatory molecule binds to this site, it induces a change in the enzyme’s shape, which in turn affects how the enzyme operates—either enhancing or reducing its activity depending on the regulator. The term regulatory site appears directly in the description of this mechanism.

text: Protein biosynthesis begins in the cell nucleus, where transcription takes place. The DNA is held within the nucleus, and RNA polymerase reads the DNA strand from the 3-prime end to the 5-prime end, synthesizing a single strand of messenger RNA in the 5'-to-3' direction. This mRNA then exits the nucleus through nuclear pores and moves into the cytoplasm, where it directs protein synthesis. In the cell nucleus, the process of transcription occurs, which is essential for producing the RNA that will eventually lead to protein formation. in the cell nucleus
title: Protein biosynthesis

text: Pseudounipolar neurons, also known as unipolar neurons, have their cell bodies situated in the dorsal root ganglion. The peripheral branch travels through the distal dorsal root into the spinal nerve, extending all the way to skin, joint, and muscle. The distal dorsal root is where the peripheral branch of the unipolar neuron is found.

text: The outermost layer of the skin, known as the epidermis, contains no blood vessels or nerve supply. It is further divided into strata including corneum, lucidum, granulosum, spinosum, and basale, with new cells formed through mitosis in the basale layer. As these cells move upward, they undergo changes in shape and composition, eventually reaching the corneum where they shed through a process called desquamation. This keratinized layer serves as a protective barrier, preventing water loss and blocking harmful substances and pathogens from entering the body. The epidermis is the correct answer.
