text: Sonnet 116 is one of Shakespeare's most famous love sonnets, and it is widely recognized for its assertion that "love is not love that alters when it alteration finds meaning." While some scholars have questioned the interpretation of this sonnet as a celebration of true love, Hilton Landry notes that though it possesses "the grandeur of generality or a 'universal significance,'" its meaning is not limitless—it has a restricted or particular range simply because it does not stand alone. Carol Thomas Neely observes that Sonnet 116 belongs to a unique sequence, alongside Sonnets 94 and 129, which differs from the rest of Shakespeare’s sonnets due to its sense of detachment and its focus on the fallibility of love. In this sequence, the poet acknowledges the imperfections of love more openly than in earlier sonnets, suggesting a more nuanced and realistic portrayal. Despite these contextual insights, critics argue that the lack of a definitive sequence makes it difficult to rely on context to determine the sonnet’s tone, and Shakespeare himself does not offer a resolution in this piece.
title: Sonnet 116

text: Advisory speed limits are indicated by yellow 35 mph signs, which serve as warnings rather than enforceable regulations. text: Fiat money serves as a medium of exchange in modern economies, though critics argue it fails to meet the essential criteria for such a role due to its free-floating nature and dependence on market supply and demand. Because fiat money’s value is not anchored to a physical commodity or intrinsic worth, it does not provide a stable or reliable standard for measuring wealth or determining just prices. As a result, its manipulation undermines the market mechanism and diminishes the purchasing power of the basket of goods and services it is linked to. This lack of stability makes fiat money an inadequate medium of exchange in the long term. In contrast, proponents such as Chartalists view the flexibility of fiat money as an advantage, particularly in enabling fiscal stimulus during economic downturns. Fiat money remains the prevailing form of currency in most economies today.
title: Medium of exchange

text: The sciatic nerve, also known as the ischiadic or ischiatic nerve, is the longest and widest single nerve in the human body. It begins in the lower back and travels through the buttock before descending down the lower limb, extending from the top of the leg to the foot on the posterior aspect. This nerve serves as the primary connection to the nervous system for the skin of the leg, the muscles of the back of the thigh, and those of the leg and foot. It originates from spinal nerves L4 to S3 and includes fibers from both the anterior and posterior divisions of the lumbosacral plexus.

text: The Highway of Heroes is a designated section of Ontario Highway 401 that begins at Glen Miller Road in Trenton and extends to Keele Street in Toronto. On August 24, 2007, the portion of the highway between Glen Miller Road in Trenton and the Don Valley Parkway / Highway 404 Junction in Toronto was designated the Highway of Heroes, as the road is travelled by funeral convoys for fallen Canadian Forces personnel from CFB Trenton to the coroner's office in Toronto. On September 27, 2013, the Highway of Heroes designation was extended west to Keele Street in Toronto, to coincide with the move of the coroner's office to the new Forensic Services and Coroner's Complex at the Humber River Hospital.
title: Ontario Highway 401

text: H. L. Hunley, often referred to as Hunley, was a submarine of the Confederate States of America that played a small part in the American Civil War. The vessel was named for her inventor, Horace Lawson Hunley, shortly after she was taken into government service under the control of the Confederate States Army at Charleston, South Carolina. Horace Lawson Hunley designed the submarine, which demonstrated the advantages and the dangers of undersea warfare. She was the first combat submarine to sink a warship (USS Housatonic), although Hunley was not completely submerged and, following her successful attack, was lost along with her crew before she could return to base. The Confederacy lost 21 crewmen in three sinkings of Hunley during her short career.
title: H. L. Hunley (submarine)

text: In the 2017 Virginia gubernatorial election, Democratic nominee Ralph Northam defeated Republican nominee Ed Gillespie, winning by the largest margin for a Democrat since 1985. Ralph Northam will become the 73rd governor of Virginia, and take office on January 13, 2018. The election saw the highest voter turnout percentage in a Virginia gubernatorial election in twenty years, with 47% of the state's constituency casting their ballot.
title: Virginia gubernatorial election, 2017

text: The University of Wisconsin–Madison, commonly referred to as UW–Madison or simply Madison, is a public research university located in Madison, Wisconsin. Founded when Wisconsin achieved statehood in 1848, it serves as the official state university and the flagship campus of the University of Wisconsin System. The 933-acre main campus includes four National Historic Landmarks.
title: University of Wisconsin–Madison

text: The signing of the United States Declaration of Independence took place on August 2, 1776 at the Pennsylvania State House, Independence Hall in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. This event marked the formal endorsement by 56 delegates to the Second Continental Congress of the Declaration of Independence, which had been approved by the Congress on July 4, 1776. The document declared that the former Thirteen Colonies, then at war with Great Britain, had become a sovereign, independent nation and were no longer part of the British Empire. The signers' names are grouped by state, with the exception of President of the Continental Congress John Hancock; the states are arranged geographically from north to south. August 2, 1776.
title: Signing of the United States Declaration of Independence

text: The final version of the Declaration of Independence was adopted by the Continental Congress on July 4, 1776, but the actual signing occurred later. Historical consensus indicates that the document was signed on August 2, 1776, nearly a month after its approval, and not on July 4 as many people assume.
title: Signing of the United States Declaration of Independence

text: Henry Purcell, an English composer born around 10 September 1659 and died on 21 November 1695, is generally considered to be one of the greatest English composers. Although his work incorporated Italian and French stylistic elements, his legacy represents a uniquely English form of Baroque music. He is generally considered to be one of the greatest English composers; no other native-born English composer approached his fame until Edward Elgar, Ralph Vaughan Williams, William Walton and Benjamin Britten in the 20th century.
title: Henry Purcell
